technology.summary: Today's technology news is dominated by the announcement of Microsoft's new AI chip, the Maia 300, which will make the company less reliant on Nvidia's GPUs. The chip is designed to be the "primary AI inference system" for Microsoft's products and services, improving the cost and efficiency of running AI workloads in the cloud. Meanwhile, Amazon has over 1 million robot workers, raising questions about the future of human employees. TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 is focused on building enduring companies in the AI era, while Fitbit has launched the Edge, a fitness tracker for those who don't want to go totally screenless.

finance.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India have teamed up to make it easier for foreign portfolio investors to enter the market. This comes as investors approach October, which is historically a positive month for the market, but which could be impacted by high crude oil prices, increasing bond yields, and continued foreign selling. A resurgent El Niño pattern risks deepening a selloff in Southeast Asian bonds, threatening to push yields higher just as rising US Treasury rates and oil prices squeeze regional debt. Indian equity benchmarks experienced a decline over two sessions due to profit booking and rising oil prices.

citations.headline: Sebi, RBI join hands to make onboarding easier for FPIs

politics.summary:
The Delhi High Court has dismissed pleas for a SIT probe into the 2020 riots and 2019 Jamia violence. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court will list a plea to allow peaceful protests at Jantar Mantar, where protesters are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

In other news, Jairam Ramesh has attacked the CEC, calling him a liability for the country, while Congress has condemned the detention of tribal students who were heading to Mumbai to protest.

Elsewhere, Donald Trump has called the US electoral process 'corrupt' in reference to an Indian election that didn't happen, and Koel Mallick has joined the BJP.

India's foreign exchange reserves have reportedly declined by $18.34 billion in a single week.
